summary: This section explains what kinds of debts and claims can be submitted when a company is being wound up or closed down. Almost all claims, whether they are certain or uncertain, present or future, are allowed to be proved against the company. A fair estimate must be made for any claims that do not have a fixed value.
points: Applies to every winding up of a company.
Allows all debts payable on a contingency to be admitted to proof.
Allows all present or future claims, whether certain or contingent, to be admitted.
Allows claims that sound only in damages to be admitted.
Requires a just estimate to be made for debts or claims that do not have a certain value.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is going through a winding up process. Rohit has a claim against the company for future damages due to a broken contract, and Anita has a claim that depends on a future uncertain event happening. Under this section, both Rohit and Anita can submit their claims to be proved against the company. The liquidator will then make a fair estimate of the value of these uncertain claims so they can be considered fairly alongside the fixed debts of the company during the closure.

terms.meaning: The legal process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.
An event that may or may not happen in the future.
The formal submission and verification of a debt or claim.
Money claimed by a person as compensation for a loss or injury.

watch: People often confuse uncertain future claims with completely invalid claims, but this section ensures even uncertain claims are allowed by estimating their value.
